subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Correction and reflection: theatre, direction, and presentation craft
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Theatre — Creating
essential_question: What choices turn a text on a page into something an audience experiences?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to correct work on theatre, direction, and presentation craft and demonstrate corrected understanding on a fresh item.
Communicate understanding of theatre, direction, and presentation craft using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on theatre, direction, and presentation craft against the stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on theatre, direction, and presentation craft.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: script, score, or devised material — public-domain or original only
private rehearsal space; no recording equipment is required at any point

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Critique and reflection work on theatre, direction, and presentation craft. Critique and reflection: organize events, marks, sounds, words, objects, or movements through theatre, direction, and presentation craft, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Set criteria before making and evaluate observable evidence against them.
primary_task: Target for this correct session: Use error evidence to correct work on theatre, direction, and presentation craft and demonstrate corrected understanding on a fresh item. Communicate understanding of theatre, direction, and presentation craft using subject-appropriate evidence or representation. Check, revise, or improve the work on theatre, direction, and presentation craft against the stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: For one corrected item, state the original error, its cause, and the check that would catch it next time. 1. Error analysis: Name the observable mismatch in earlier work without judging taste or effort. Locate it, compare it with the stated criterion, and choose the smallest useful repair. 2. Supported revision: Test the repair on a separate small study before changing the scored work. Use a different cue or representation and record what the test reveals. 3. Fresh transfer: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan. Record what the fresh evidence shows; keep the earlier attempt without penalty. Your choices remain yours: Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about theatre, direction, and presentation craft, and it belongs to "Theatre, Direction, and Presentation Craft", which also covers separate topics such as script analysis of public-domain or original text. Close out with this check before you stop: For one corrected item, state the original error, its cause, and the check that would catch it next time. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

critique_criteria: The submission contains the alternate explanation, supported attempt, and new transfer; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting theatre, direction, and presentation craft.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce theatre, direction, and presentation craft to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply theatre, direction, and presentation craft under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on theatre, direction, and presentation craft rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on theatre, direction, and presentation craft.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

a purposeful version made to test one choice

concept_instruction.title: What theatre, direction, and presentation craft means here
concept_instruction.body: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: Moving between media can reveal structure but may change the measured skill; name which evidence transfers and which does not. Worked example: Short → short-short → long can be drawn, tapped, moved, or silently counted while preserving its pattern of arrival, urgency, and rest. Non-example: Switching media and changing every relationship at once makes it impossible to tell what caused the new effect.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in theatre, direction, and presentation craft.
technique_sequence.why: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for theatre, direction, and presentation craft is present, but the record does not yet locate sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
